description.value:
Normalized BBTTCC ancestry. This item keeps the original species UUID while fitting the ancestry-root layer of the new identity stack.

“The land is not scenery. The land is a person. You are the version of it that finally stood up and walked over to complain.”

Menhirkin. You are not descended from the land. You are the land. A hex decided to become a person and the person is you. The standing stones on the ridge are distant cousins. The bedrock under the bunker is a grandparent. Every place that has ever had a will of its own is, in some sense, family.

Menhirkin are the walking, talking expression of sentient land—the ley-grid made ambulatory, the bunker given opinions, the standing stone that finally got tired of standing. Mortals call you a Hex-Giant. You don’t correct them, because the name is not wrong so much as it is incomplete.

You do not hold territory. Territory holds you, and moves where you move.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin).
  • Size. You are Medium, but you count as Large for determining your carrying capacity and the size of creatures you can shove or grapple.
  • Speed. Your walking speed is 30 feet.
  • Ability Scores. Your background determines your ability score increases; Menhirkin does not grant any ability score bonuses.
  • Heartstone. A fragment of your home hex is literally inside you. While in any hex your faction controls or has claimed, you gain advantage on Constitution saves and cannot be forcibly removed from the hex against your will (teleportation, banishment, or forced march) without first being reduced to 0 hp.
  • Land Memory. You can lay a hand on any surface older than you and ask it what has happened there. The GM answers with one true thing the land remembers. Once per long rest.
  • Living Rampart. You have proficiency in the Athletics skill. As a reaction when a creature you can see targets an ally adjacent to you with an attack, you can interpose bulk and bad life choices, imposing disadvantage on that attack roll. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
  • Stonebound. You have advantage on ability checks you make to resist being pushed, knocked prone, or otherwise forcibly moved. You also have advantage on checks you make to build, repair, or fortify structures, siegeworks, and defensive emplacements.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / BBTTCC)

“Congratulations, the bunker took a level in you.”

  • OP Edge. Your faction gains +2 Non-Lethal OP and +1 Violence OP at campaign start.
  • Fortify Hex. Each Turn, the first Patch the Breach or structure-repair Siege activity your faction undertakes costs 1 fewer OP (minimum 0).
  • Logistics Frame. Once per Turn, when your faction runs a raid or operation with a Logistics cost, you can treat that cost as Logistics −1 (minimum 0) as you move siege materials like they’re foam props.
  • Sentient Land. Once per Strategic Turn, while standing on a hex your faction controls, you can consult the hex itself about a pending decision. The GM provides a one-sentence answer from the land’s perspective (not the faction’s). It is always honest. It is rarely comforting.

senses.special: Tremorsense 10 ft while standing on natural ground.
